description:
AEGIS – Every Marswalk Deserves a Way Home

AEGIS is an innovative concept that uses NASA's open data to make Mars exploration safer and smarter. By combining terrain analysis, scientific priorities, and risk assessment, it aims to help astronauts choose safer routes, identify valuable exploration sites, and plan alternative paths in emergencies.

AEGIS goes beyond mapping Mars: it helps astronauts explore confidently and return safely.
summary:
AEGIS – Every Marswalk Deserves a Way Home

AEGIS (Adaptive Exploration & Ground Intelligence System) is an innovative concept for an intelligent Mars navigation system designed to support safer and more efficient human exploration.

Our project proposes combining NASA's open datasets, including satellite imagery, topographic maps, and geological information, to identify scientifically valuable destinations, assess terrain hazards, and plan exploration routes.

Unlike traditional mapping tools, AEGIS introduces uncertainty-aware navigation and adaptive return planning. It aims to evaluate the reliability of available data, highlight potential risks, and suggest alternative routes when unexpected obstacles or emergencies occur.

AEGIS addresses the challenge by transforming complex Martian data into actionable information that could help astronauts make better decisions during surface missions.

Our vision is to make Mars exploration safer, smarter, and more scientifically productive, ensuring that every journey has a plan for a safe return.
